subject: HealthMax — Request for SLA exhibit and order-form language for uptime/latency exceptions
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita@healthmax.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, procurement@healthmax.com
Date: 2027-03-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: New: SLA exhibit / availability windows for Redwood deployment

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward signature on the MSA + order form, our procurement and engineering teams flagged a couple of items we need to lock down in an SLA exhibit and the order form language. I attached our highlighted RFP section but pulled the asks into bullets below so you have a quick view.

Key asks:
- Target monthly uptime: 99.95% for production; need definition of measurement period and calculation (calendar month).
- Latency commitments: p50/p95 for text generation at 512 tokens; provide expected ranges for both hosted and dedicated variants.
- Exception carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (max 4 hours/month) + emergency maintenance — define notice windows and blackout periods.
- Data locality & residency: logs/metrics must be stored in AWS-us-east-1 for our audit needs.
- Proofs: SOC 2 report + 30 days of retention for audit logs to be made available upon request.
- Fallback: if Redwood cannot meet the committed availability, we need defined remediation (credits) and a short-term dedicated pool option for burst capacity.

Can you please provide a proposed SLA exhibit and any redlineable order form language? Procurement would also like to know whether Redwood can accept a 60-day contract signing cadence with an initial 6-month pilot and what the dedicated pool pricing looks like.

Attachments: HealthMax_RFP_SLA_requirements.pdf (pdf) | HealthMax_MSA_draft_20270320.docx (docx)

Best,
Anita Shah
Director, Procurement
HealthMax
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita@healthmax.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New: SLA exhibit / availability windows for Redwood deployment

Hi Anita —

Thanks for sending this and for the clear bullets — extremely helpful. I attached our standard SLA addendum template and will work with Ben (contracts/pricing) and Laura (procurement sequencing) to put together two paths:

1) Hosted path: proposed SLA language, expected latency bands at 512 tokens (p50/p95), and standard credit matrix.
2) Dedicated option: proposed dedicated pool pricing and SLA uplift language (short-term dedicated capacity for failover).

A few quick clarifications before we redline:
- For the monthly uptime calculation, do you require rolling 30-day windows or calendar months? Procurement said calendar months but want to confirm.
- For data locality, is retention of audit logs in us-east-1 sufficient or do you require all telemetry to never leave us-east-1?

I'll circulate a draft SLA exhibit and annotated order form language by EOD tomorrow. If HealthMax legal prefers, we can accept DocuSign or a redlined Word doc from Paul O'Connor — please loop him in.

Next steps: Ben will scope pricing & dedicated pool delta; Laura will outline procurement steps and timeline.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Template_v2.docx]
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita@healthmax.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New: SLA exhibit / availability windows for Redwood deployment

Hi Anita — looping in pricing and procurement logistics as promised. Quick notes from our side:

- Uptime: We can support a 99.95% monthly uptime SLA for the hosted tier. For dedicated deployments, we can commit to 99.97% conditional on reserved capacity and network topology review.
- Measurement period: Redwood prefers calendar month for billing/credits; rolling 30-day windows add operational complexity but is negotiable.
- Latency: p50/p95 at 512 tokens (hosted): ~25ms / ~160ms server-side token generation (doesn't include network RTT). For dedicated pools on current GPU types (A100-equivalent), p50/p95 ~18ms / ~120ms. We'll put these as expected ranges and note they vary by prompt shape and batching.
- Maintenance: Standard scheduled maintenance windows are up to 4 hours/month with 72-hour notice for planned major upgrades; emergency maintenance will be used sparingly and we'll provide post-incident reports.
- Credits: Standard credit band: <99.0% = 30% credit; 99.0-99.5% = 15%; 99.5-99.95% = 5%. For dedicated pools we can propose steeper credits depending on commit.

Dedicated pool pricing: I'll attach a small pricing summary and a pilot option (6-week pilot with pro-rated commit and option to convert).

Items we need from HealthMax to finalize the draft:
- Confirm calendar month vs rolling 30-day window.
- Clarify exact audit log retention & location requirement (us-east-1 only vs preferred).
- Confirm whether the pilot will require HIPAA BAA scope (if yes, security team will engage).

Attachments: redlines_healthmax_orderform_stephanie_20270322.docx (will include pricing table)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
From: Anita Shah <anita@healthmax.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul O'Connor <poconnor@medlegal.com>, procurement@healthmax.com
Date: 2027-03-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New: SLA exhibit / availability windows for Redwood deployment

Thanks, Ben and Stephanie — this is a good start. A couple of clarifications from procurement & engineering after reviewing your notes:

- Calendar month is preferred for credits and reporting.
- For data locality: we require audit logs and metrics to remain in us-east-1 for retention and eDiscovery purposes; operational telemetry that crosses regions for routing is acceptable as long as logs/metrics storage is in us-east-1.
- Pilot duration: procurement would like a 6-month pilot (to align with our internal Q3 pilot calendar), with the option to convert earlier if metrics look good. Can Redwood accommodate a 6-month initial pilot with monthly performance reviews?
- HIPAA: HealthMax will treat this as PHI-adjacent; we will send a formal BAA request if we proceed to production.

Paul (HealthMax legal) — looping you in for redlines on order form language and the MSA exhibit.

Best,
Anita
From: Paul O'Connor <poconnor@medlegal.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Anita Shah <anita@healthmax.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-22T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: HealthMax redlines: SLA exhibit and order form — summary

Stephanie / Ben —

Attached are HealthMax's redlines to the Redwood SLA addendum and the order form. Summary of the principal legal asks:

1) Clear definition of measurement methodology: calendar month, UTC, specifying excluded windows (scheduled maint, force majeure).
2) Remedies: liquidated credits as agreed; we propose an incremental credit ladder and cap at 100% of fees for the affected month only.
3) Availability exceptions: narrower notice for scheduled maintenance (48 hours) and a requirement for at least one 30-day maintenance blackout avoidance per quarter.
4) Audit & data residency: audit logs retained in us-east-1 for 24 months; Redwood to provide read-only access to named HealthMax auditors on request.
5) Dedicated pool fallback: request explicit conversion pricing and an SLA uplift schedule if HealthMax purchases a reserved pool within 30 days of an availability breach.

We also attached a redlined order form that integrates the credit matrix and a proposed cadence for monthly performance reviews during the pilot. Please review the attached and confirm a path to accept or further negotiate each bullet.

Attachments: HealthMax_MSA_draft_20270320.docx (with comments) | HealthMax_redlines_SLA_OrderForm_20270322.docx

Paul O'Connor
Senior Counsel, MedLegal Advisors (external counsel to HealthMax)
